title: Weierstrass division and preparation with Gauss-norm bounds
statement:
Let $F$ be a complete field with a nontrivial real-valued nonarchimedean absolute value. For any finite list of variables $Z$, define $F\langle Zangle$ as the ring of series $\sum_
u c_
u Z^
u$ with only finitely many $|c_
u|\ge\epsilon$ for every $\epsilon>0$, with Gauss norm $\sup_
u|c_
u|$. Let $s\ge0$, $A=F\langle Y_1,\ldots,Y_sangle$, and $D=F\langle Y_1,\ldots,Y_s,Xangle$. Write $g=\sum_{i\ge0}a_iX^i\in D$. Suppose $d\ge0$, $a_d=1$, $\|a_i\|\le1$ for $i<d$, and $\sup_{i>d}\|a_i\|<1$. For every $h\in D$ there is a unique pair $q\in D$, $r\in A[X]$ [def-weil-polynomial-ring] of degree less than $d$ such that $h=qg+r$, and $\|q\|,\|r\|\le\|h\|$. Furthermore $g=u w$ for a monic $w\in A[X]$ of degree $d$ whose lower coefficients have norm at most $1$, and a unit $u\in D$ with $\|u\|,\|u^{-1}\|\le1$. For $d=0$ the remainder is zero and $w=1$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-restricted-series-gauss-completion] with $n=s,s+1$. Thus $A$ and $D$ are complete, their norms satisfy the strong triangle inequality and submultiplicativity, and $D$ is isometrically the restricted series $\sum a_iX^i$ over $A$. Let $E=A[X]_{<d}$, meaning the polynomials [def-weil-polynomial-ring] supported in $0,\ldots,d-1$, with the maximum coefficient norm. For $d=0$ set $E=\{0\}$. Coefficientwise limits make $E=A^d$ complete, and its inclusion in $D$ is isometric. Put $p=X^d+\sum_{i<d}a_iX^i$ and $e=g-p$. Then $\|p\|=1$ and $c=\|e\|=\sup_{i>d}\|a_i\|<1$, with $c=0$ when $e=0$.

source.place: Setup: Gauss completion and regrouping, then the polynomial part and small upper tail. Agent reconstruction: the BGR book is WANTED and no precise theorem number is claimed.

proof.text: First divide only polynomials by $p$, using the finite-support definition [def-weil-polynomial-ring]. Induct on the degree $N$ of a polynomial $b$. If $b=0$ or $N<d$, take quotient $0$ and remainder $b$. Otherwise let $\beta$ be its leading coefficient and replace $b$ by $b'=b-\beta X^{N-d}p$, whose degree is smaller than $N$. The norm estimates in step 1 give $\|b'\|\le\|b\|$, because $\|p\|=1$ and $\|\beta X^{N-d}\|\le\|b\|$. An inductively constructed pair $v',t'$ for $b'$ gives $v=v'+\beta X^{N-d}$ and $t=t'$, both of norm at most $\|b\|$. Uniqueness is a coefficient calculation: for nonzero polynomial $v$, monicity gives $\deg(pv)=d+\deg v$, which cannot equal a polynomial in $E$. Subtract two decompositions. Write $Q(b),R(b)$ for this unique pair; uniqueness also proves additivity and $A$-linearity. If $d=0$, $p=1$, and the formulas are $Q(b)=b$, $R(b)=0$.

source.place: Elementary finite descending-degree division algorithm with its coefficient norm bound. Agent reconstruction: the BGR book is WANTED and no precise theorem number is claimed.

proof.text: Extend these particular polynomial operators explicitly. For $b=\sum b_iX^i\in D$, set $b^{(N)}=\sum_{i=0}^Nb_iX^i$. Regrouping in [lem-trf-restricted-series-gauss-completion] gives $\|b-b^{(N)}\|\to0$. Additivity and step 2 give $\|Q(b^{(M)})-Q(b^{(N)})\|,\|R(b^{(M)})-R(b^{(N)})\|\le\|b^{(M)}-b^{(N)}\|$. Completeness of $D$ and $E$ therefore defines limits $Q_0(b),R_0(b)$. The same estimate shows independence of any polynomial approximating sequence, additivity, $A$-linearity and $\|Q_0(b)\|,\|R_0(b)\|\le\|b\|$. Passing to the limit in $b^{(N)}=pQ(b^{(N)})+R(b^{(N)})$ gives $b=pQ_0(b)+R_0(b)$; multiplication by fixed $p$ is continuous since $\|p(x-y)\|\le\|x-y\|$. Also, for $v\in D$ and $t\in E$, the polynomial identities $Q(pv^{(N)}+t)=v^{(N)}$ and $R(pv^{(N)}+t)=t$ pass to the limit, so $Q_0(pv+t)=v$ and $R_0(pv+t)=t$. In particular $Q_0(X^d)=1$ and $Q_0(t)=0$ for $t\in E$.

source.place: Construct the bounded division operators from X-truncations and complete coefficient limits; verify both inverse identities. Agent reconstruction: the BGR book is WANTED and no precise theorem number is claimed.

proof.text: For the given $h$, set $h_0=h$ and, successively, $v_j=Q_0(h_j)$, $t_j=R_0(h_j)$, $h_{j+1}=-ev_j$. From step 3, $h_j=gv_j+t_j+h_{j+1}$. Induction gives $\|h_j\|\le c^j\|h\|$ and $\|v_j\|,\|t_j\|\le c^j\|h\|$. If $c=0$, all terms after $j=0$ vanish; otherwise $0<c<1$ and $c^j\to0$. For $M\ge N$, the strong triangle inequality bounds the norm of $\sum_{j=N}^Mv_j$, and likewise of $\sum_{j=N}^Mt_j$, by $c^N\|h\|$. Hence the sums converge in $D$ and $E$ by [lem-trf-restricted-series-gauss-completion] and the finite-coordinate completeness of step 1. Denote them by $q$ and $r$. Every partial sum has norm at most $\|h\|$, and this bound passes to its limit. Summing the displayed recursion through $j=N$ gives $h=g\sum_{j=0}^Nv_j+\sum_{j=0}^Nt_j+h_{N+1}$. The last term tends to zero. Continuity of multiplication by $g$, using $\|g(x-y)\|\le\|g\|\|x-y\|$, gives $h=gq+r$ and the claimed norm bounds.

source.place: Contracting correction for the small upper tail, with explicit finite-sum identity and convergence estimates. Agent reconstruction: the BGR book is WANTED and no precise theorem number is claimed.

proof.text: For uniqueness, subtract two decompositions and write $0=gv+t=pv+t+ev$ with $v\in D$, $t\in E$. Apply the additive operator $Q_0$ and the identity $Q_0(pv+t)=v$ from step 3. It follows that $v=-Q_0(ev)$ and $\|v\|\le c\|v\|$. Since $0\le c<1$ and norms are nonnegative real numbers, $\|v\|=0$, hence $v=0$ and then $t=0$. This applies to arbitrary decompositions, without assuming any norm bounds on them.

source.place: Elementary uniqueness from the strict contraction inequality already established. Agent reconstruction: the BGR book is WANTED and no precise theorem number is claimed.

proof.text: Apply the division just proved to $X^d$, whose norm is $1$. Write $X^d=bg+r_*$ with $r_*\in E$ and $\|b\|,\|r_*\|\le1$. Applying $Q_0$ gives $1=b+Q_0(eb)$, because $g=p+e$ and $Q_0(r_*)=0$. Thus $\|1-b\|\le c<1$. Set $z=1-b$. To check invertibility explicitly, the finite sums $S_N=\sum_{k=0}^Nz^k$ satisfy $\|S_M-S_N\|\le\|z\|^{N+1}$ for $M>N$ and $\|S_N\|\le1$. By [lem-trf-restricted-series-gauss-completion] they converge to $S\in D$ of norm at most $1$ (for $z=0$ take $S=1$). The finite identities $(1-z)S_N=S_N(1-z)=1-z^{N+1}$ pass to the limit by the product norm bound. Therefore $bS=Sb=1$. Put $w=X^d-r_*$ and $u=S=b^{-1}$; then $bg=w$, so $g=uw$. The polynomial $w$ is monic of degree $d$, with lower coefficient norms at most $1$, and $\|u\|\le1$ and $\|u^{-1}\|=\|b\|\le1$.

source.place: Preparation from the division of X^d; the near-identity quotient is inverted by explicit geometric sums. Agent reconstruction: the BGR book is WANTED and no precise theorem number is claimed.

proof.text: When $d=0$, $E=\{0\}$ throughout: the division remainder is zero, the prepared polynomial in step 6 is $X^0-0=1$, and $g=u$ is a unit with the stated bounds. When $h=0$, the construction has every $h_j,v_j,t_j$ zero, so $q=r=0$. When $s=0$, all coefficient limits occur in $A=F$ and the same argument applies. If the upper tail is zero, the correction in step 4 stops after its first term. Thus none of these edge cases uses a positive-degree, positive-tail or additional-variable assumption.
